about: Hand-curated list prices for paid nodes. Every entry cites the vendor page and the date it was checked. See services/model_pricing.py for the format; never add a price without a canonical source.

gpt-image-2-5-edit.notes: Output image tokens at $30/1M, per OpenAI's image-cost calculator on its docs (sizes OpenAI doesn't tabulate are computed with the same formula). 'auto' quality or size is left to the API, which picks per image, so those settings show a range. Text input is negligible; one image per run (the handler streams, so n is never sent). Edits also bill each input image and mask as image input tokens ($8/1M); OpenAI publishes no token formula for GPT Image 2/2.5 inputs, so that part isn't estimated.

sources.quote: gpt-image-2.5-flare | $8.00 image input | $30.00 image output (per 1M tokens, Standard)
Use explicit quality and size values for this estimate; auto depends on the generated image.

jev-box.notes: One request holding the image once and two questions (is it there, and where). TypeSafe bills input tokens only ($0.042 per million; output is free) and images as input tokens, with no published per-image count yet; its own example of one image and a Box question is about 290 tokens. One request can't exceed the 64k-token context limit, so the high end is that limit. Failed requests are assumed not to bill.

sources.quote: Jev 1.14 and 1.13: $0.042 per Mtok of input; output tokens free; context 64k per request / 32k per question
Image tokens are billed at the input token price; no separate image charge

jev-decide.notes: TypeSafe bills input tokens only ($0.042 per million; output is free) and images as input tokens, with no published per-image count yet. One request can't exceed the context limit, so the high end is that limit: 64k tokens by default, 262k with Long context. The low end is a short text-only question (~250 tokens). Failed requests are assumed not to bill.

sources.quote: Jev 1.14 and 1.13: $0.042 per Mtok of input; output tokens free; context 64k per request / 32k per question
Long context header: 262k per request and per question, same price per token
Image tokens are billed at the input token price; no separate image charge

jev-pick-best.notes: One Choice request over every candidate. TypeSafe bills input tokens only ($0.042 per million; output is free) and images as input tokens, with no published per-image count yet. One request can't exceed the 64k-token context limit, so the high end is that limit. The low end is two small candidates. Failed requests are assumed not to bill; a request over the limit is sent once more with smaller candidates.

kling-v3.notes: fal list price per generated second (text-to-video route the handler always uses). Multi-prompt runs are unpriced: Kling requires the shot durations to sum to the total, but neither fal nor Kling says whether a mismatched sum is rejected or billed by the shots. Voice control ($0.154/s) is not reachable from this node's schema.

nano-banana.notes: Gemini API standard (paid tier) output-image prices. Nano Banana 2.1 (Interactions API) has 1K/2K/4K only and renders a saved 512 at 1K. The handler renders 512 on 3 Pro as 1K, Flash-Lite always at 1K, and sends no size for 2.5 Flash. Input text and reference images add well under $0.01. Ignores Batch/Flex/Priority rates.

Equivalent to $0.134 per 1K/2K image and $0.24 per 4K image
Output images up to 1024x1024px consume 1290 tokens and are equivalent to $0.039 per image.

nano-banana-fal.notes: fal list price per image. Pro bills 0.5K as 1K (the handler bumps it) and lists no 2K premium. Nano Banana, 2.5 Flash Image and Gemini 3 Pro Image ignore resolution, web search and thinking here (the handler strips them). fal doesn't say whether the web-search and thinking add-ons are per request or per image; they're counted per image, the higher reading.

veo-3.notes: Google routes only (Vertex service-account key or GOOGLE_API_KEY); the fal fallback is unpriced. Per second of the node's duration and resolution (defaults 8 s, 720p); audio is always generated, so these are the with-audio prices. Vertex lists the same amounts per "count" without saying what a count is; they are read as per second here, the higher reading. An extension renders at 720p whatever the setting. Lite has no 4K. Billed only when the video generates.
